title: Personal Project Ideas: Sustainability for MYP
summary: Personal Project ideas for sustainability, with nine practical topics, clear learning and product goals, success criteria, and a complete MYP example.
body_markdown:
The strongest **Personal Project ideas for sustainability** connect one environmental problem with a skill you want to learn and a product you can evaluate. A torn shirt or overflowing lunch bin can provide a starting point. The challenge is choosing something small enough to investigate carefully.


For an MYP Year 5 student, sustainability is an interest, but it is not yet a goal. Your project involves a process, a product or outcome, and a reflective report. Start with RevisionDojo's guide to[what the MYP Personal Project involves](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-is-the-myp-personal-project) if those elements feel unfamiliar.


### A quick sustainability project checklist


Before choosing, ask:


- What knowledge or skill will I develop?
- What will I create, and for whom?
- Can I access the necessary time, materials, and permissions?
- How will I test the result?
- What evidence will show my planning and reflection?


A learning goal explains what you intend to learn. A product goal explains what you intend to create using that learning. See[how to write a strong Personal Project goal](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/strong-myp-personal-project-goal) for further guidance.


### Nine Personal Project ideas for sustainability


### Create an upcycled clothing collection


**Learn:** Garment construction, repair techniques, and how clothing choices affect material use and waste.


**Create:** Three wearable pieces from unwanted garments, documenting sketches, construction, and testing.


Keep the collection manageable. Test comfort and durability, then record how feedback changes your designs.


### Design a food-waste reduction campaign


**Learn:** Waste auditing, data interpretation, and persuasive environmental communication.


**Create:** A campaign for one household, class, or school group over a defined period.


Measure waste before and after using the same method, such as mass or item counts. Protect participants' privacy and acknowledge other possible explanations for changes.


### Build a beginner composting system


**Learn:** How air, moisture, material balance, and particle size affect aerobic decomposition.


**Create:** A suitable composting system and a user guide based on observations.


Obtain permission and check local safety guidance. Evaluate the system's operation without promising finished compost by a fixed date, since decomposition times vary.


### Produce a native pollinator garden plan


**Learn:** How locally appropriate plants, seasonal flowering, and habitat features support pollinators.


**Create:** A site-specific plan with scale drawings, plant choices, maintenance guidance, and a budget.


Consult reliable local sources. A digital design is practical when planting is unavailable; plants suitable for one region may be unsuitable elsewhere.


### Develop a household energy dashboard


**Learn:** Electricity measurement and clear data presentation.


**Create:** A spreadsheet or dashboard showing usage patterns and realistic conservation actions.


Use bills, adult-approved smart-meter information, or sample data. Avoid handling electrical equipment. Evaluate whether your intended audience understands the charts and recommendations.


### Make a repair guide for everyday objects


**Learn:** Safe repair methods, documentation, and instructional design.


**Create:** A photo or video guide covering three to five repairs, tested by intended users.


Choose low-risk objects such as clothing or books. Record where readers struggle and revise the instructions accordingly.


### Design sustainable packaging


**Learn:** Packaging functions, material trade-offs, prototyping, and life-cycle thinking.


**Create:** Three prototypes for one specific product, with an evidence-based final recommendation.


Test protection, material quantity, opening, reuse potential, and disposal instructions. Explain trade-offs rather than assuming one material is always preferable.


### Create a water-conscious garden model


**Learn:** How plant selection, soil covering, and irrigation design affect water demand.


**Create:** A physical or digital model for a defined school space, including calculations and maintenance instructions.


State the assumptions behind estimated water use. Separate measured results from predictions so your evaluation remains credible.


### Write a sustainable eating recipe booklet


**Learn:** Researching food choices while considering nutrition, cost, culture, and availability.


**Create:** Eight tested recipes for a defined audience, including costs and feedback.


Explain your selection principles. Avoid declaring one diet universally sustainable because environmental impacts depend on location and production methods, among other factors.


Explore[more MYP Personal Project topics](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/good-myp-personal-project-topics) and[Personal Project examples for inspiration](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/real-examples-of-ib-myp-personal-projects-for-inspiration) , then adapt an idea to your circumstances.

### Turning one idea into a complete project


Imagine a hypothetical student, Lina, who enjoys fashion and notices damaged clothes sitting unused at home. She turns that observation into two connected goals.


**Learning goal:** Learn hand-sewing, machine-sewing, patching, and redesign techniques that extend clothing's usable life.


**Product goal:** Redesign three damaged garments into wearable pieces and create a beginner repair guide.


Her success criteria could require:


- Three completed garments using at least three researched techniques.
- Each garment remaining intact during an agreed wear test.
- Materials lists, safety notes, photographs, and ordered instructions.
- Structured guide feedback from at least three intended users.


These criteria assess function, quality, and audience needs. RevisionDojo's guide to the[MYP Personal Project criteria](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-personal-project-criteria) helps connect these decisions with planning, applying skills, and reflection.


Lina schedules research, practice on scrap fabric, sketches, construction, testing, feedback, and revisions. She saves dated photographs, source evaluations, rejected designs, and results. Each record should explain a decision or demonstrate learning.


Reading about[common Personal Project mistakes](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/common-myp-personal-project-mistakes-e0513f75) can help her avoid starting production too early or evaluating from memory.


### Make the project yours


Choose a problem you can observe and make the challenge come from learning. A small product tested carefully gives you specific evidence to analyse.


RevisionDojo brings wider IB support together through its Coursework Library, Study Notes, Flashcards, Questionbank, AI Chat, Grading tools, Predicted Papers, Mock Exams, and Tutors. Its guide to[how the Personal Project is graded](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-is-the-myp-personal-project-graded) can help you review whether your evidence explains your process.


Your project needs a clear promise: investigate thoughtfully, develop a skill, create something useful, and evaluate honestly. Start there, and sustainability becomes a practical question you can explore.
